title: Compatible coefficient DVRs for the complete Epp pair
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $A\to B$ be an injective local map of complete discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, $M=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ [def-pc-field-extension], $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$, and $l=B/\mathfrak m_B$. Suppose $k$ is algebraically closed (every nonconstant polynomial has a root) of characteristic $p$ and, inside $l$, $k=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\{x^{p^n}:x\in l\}$. Fix a uniformizer $\pi$ of $A$. Then there are complete discrete valuation rings $A_0,D$, injective local maps $A_0\to A$, $A_0\to D$, $D\to B$, and a commutative square with the given $A\to B$, such that: $A_0/\mathfrak m_{A_0}=k$ compatibly with $A_0\to A$; $D/\mathfrak m_D=l$ compatibly with $D\to B$; the residue map of $A_0\to D$ is the given $k\hookrightarrow l$; $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D=\mathfrak m_D$; and $B$ is a finite $D$-module (finitely many elements span it over $D$). Thus $M/\operatorname{Frac}(D)$ is finite-dimensional. If $K$ has characteristic $p$, one may choose $A_0=k[[t]]$ with $t\mapsto\pi$ and $A_0\to A$ an isomorphism; $k[[t]]$ denotes the ring of formal power series in one variable [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. If $K$ has characteristic zero, one may choose $A_0$ and $D$ to be Cohen rings [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] for $k$ and $l$, respectively (complete DVRs with uniformizer the integer $p$). Local means pulling back maximal ideals. No finite generation of $l/k$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09F9, theorem-epp, proof paragraphs setting k equal to the perfect core, choosing a Cohen ring or k[[t]], and choosing the upper coefficient DVR Lambda before the reduction to Tag 09F8. These paragraphs use Cohen structure and adic lifting; this statement records their compatible structural construction, not existence of an Epp extension.

proof.text: Choose a Cohen ring $C$ with a specified residue isomorphism $C/pC\cong k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-rings-exist]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-ring-lift-complete-local] to $R=A$ and this isomorphism to obtain $c:C\to A$ inducing the identity on $k$. If $\operatorname{char}K=0$, put $A_0=C$. The map is local: an element reduces to zero in $A$ exactly when its class in $C/pC$ is zero. It is injective, since a nonzero element of the DVR $C$ is $up^n$ with $u$ a unit and its image is nonzero in the characteristic-zero domain $A$. If $\operatorname{char}K=p$, the map $c$ kills $p$ and factors through the specified quotient $C/pC=k$, giving a section $s:k\to A$ of the residue map. This field map is injective.

source.place: Tag 09F9, theorem-epp, the two coefficient-DVR preparation paragraphs before lemma-special-case; supporting Tags 0328, 032A, 07NJ, 09E7 and 031D.

proof.text: In characteristic $p$, put $A_0=k[[t]]$ and $D=l[[t]]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] with one variable these are complete Noetherian local domains with maximal ideal $(t)$ and residue fields $k,l$. Since $t\ne0$, [lem-sc-principal-ideal-dvr] makes them DVRs. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-adic-evaluation] with coefficient map $s:k\to A$, ideal $\mathfrak m_A$ and $t\mapsto\pi$ to construct $a:A_0\to A$. This is an isomorphism: for $x\in A$, recursively choose $a_n\in k$ as the residue of $x_n$, starting with $x_0=x$, and put $x_{n+1}=(x_n-s(a_n))/\pi$. Then $x-\sum_{i<N}s(a_i)\pi^i\in\pi^NA$ for every $N$, so completeness and the evaluation formula give $x=a(\sum a_it^i)$. If a nonzero series has first nonzero coefficient $a_n$, its image is $\pi^n$ times an element with nonzero residue $a_n$, hence is nonzero. Apply the same evaluation lemma to the coefficient inclusion $k\hookrightarrow l\hookrightarrow D$ with $t\mapsto t$ to obtain $h:A_0\to D$. Its residue map is the given inclusion; it is local and injective by the same first-nonzero-coefficient argument, and $h(t)=t$ gives $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D=\mathfrak m_D$.

source.place: Tag 09F9, theorem-epp, the two coefficient-DVR preparation paragraphs before lemma-special-case; supporting Tags 0328, 032A, 07NJ, 09E7 and 031D.

proof.text: In characteristic zero choose a Cohen ring $D$ with specified residue $D/pD=l$ using [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-rings-exist]. The zero-variable Cohen case of [lem-weil-pbc-field-cohen-power-series-formally-smooth] says that $\mathbf Z\to A_0$ is formally smooth for the $(p)$-adic topology. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete] with base $R=\mathbf Z$, source $S=A_0$, target ring $D$, $I=J=pD$, and residue map $A_0\to k\hookrightarrow l=D/pD$. Here $D$ is $I$-adically complete, $J$ is closed since $J+I^m=J$, $J^1\subseteq I$, and the residue map kills $\mathfrak m_{A_0}$, so $r=t=1$ suffice in the lifting lemma. We obtain $h:A_0\to D$ with the prescribed residue map. It sends the integer $p$ to $p$, so it preserves uniformizers and $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D=\mathfrak m_D$. It is local by the injectivity of $k\to l$, and injective because a nonzero element $up^n$ has nonzero image in the domain $D$.

source.place: Tag 09F9, theorem-epp, the two coefficient-DVR preparation paragraphs before lemma-special-case; supporting Tags 0328, 032A, 07NJ, 09E7 and 031D.

proof.text: For each $x\in k$, the polynomial $X^p-x$ has a root in the algebraically closed field $k$. Thus every element of $k$ is a $p$th power. For every finitely generated subextension $E/k$ inside $l$, [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis] supplies a separating transcendence basis. Consequently $l/k$ is separable in exactly the possibly transcendental sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]; there is no hypothesis that $l/k$ itself be finitely generated. The map $h$ constructed in the relevant characteristic case is an injective local DVR map with index one and residue extension $l/k$. Hence [lem-sfb-dvr-index-one-adic-formal-smoothness] shows that $D$ is formally smooth over $A_0$ for the $\mathfrak m_D$-adic topology.

source.place: Tag 09F9, theorem-epp, the two coefficient-DVR preparation paragraphs before lemma-special-case; supporting Tags 0328, 032A, 07NJ, 09E7 and 031D.

proof.text: Give $B$ its $A_0$-algebra structure through $a:A_0\to A\to B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete] with $R=A_0$, $S=D$, target ring $B$, $I=J=\mathfrak m_B$, and $g:D\to D/\mathfrak m_D=l=B/\mathfrak m_B$. This is an $A_0$-algebra map since both residue maps restrict to the specified $k\hookrightarrow l$. Completeness of $B$ gives the $I$-adic hypothesis; $J+I^m=J$ proves closedness; $J^1\subseteq I$ and $g(\mathfrak m_D)=0$ give $t=r=1$. The lemma produces an $A_0$-algebra map $b:D\to B$ with residue identity, so $bh=A_0\to A\to B$, proving the required square. This map is local. For the common uniformizer $q=p$ in mixed characteristic or $q=t$ in equal characteristic, $b(q)$ is respectively $p\ne0$ in $B$ or the given image of $\pi\ne0$. Thus a nonzero $uq^n\in D$ cannot map to zero, and $b$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 09F9, theorem-epp, the two coefficient-DVR preparation paragraphs before lemma-special-case; supporting Tags 0328, 032A, 07NJ, 09E7 and 031D.

proof.text: Write $q$ for this uniformizer of $D$. Since $b$ is injective and local, in the DVR $B$ one can write $b(q)=u\beta^e$ for a uniformizer $\beta$, a unit $u$, and an integer $e\ge1$. Then $qB=\mathfrak m_B^e$. The classes of $1,\beta,\ldots,\beta^{e-1}$ generate $B/qB$ over $D/qD=l$: given $x\in B$, choose $d_0\in D$ with the same residue as $x$, divide $x-b(d_0)$ by $\beta$, choose $d_1$ with the residue of the quotient, and repeat $e$ times. This gives $x-\sum_{i<e}b(d_i)\beta^i\in\beta^eB=qB$. Moreover $\bigcap_nq^nB=\bigcap_n\mathfrak m_B^{en}=0$, since completeness of $B$ includes separatedness and $en$ is cofinal. The ring $D$ is $(q)$-adically complete. Thus all three hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring] hold for $A=D$, $I=qD$, $M=B$, and $B$ is finite over $D$.

source.place: Tag 09F9, theorem-epp, the two coefficient-DVR preparation paragraphs before lemma-special-case; supporting Tags 0328, 032A, 07NJ, 09E7 and 031D.

proof.text: Put $F=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$. Localizing a finite spanning set of $B$ over $D$ shows that $T=F\otimes_DB=(D\setminus\{0\})^{-1}B\subseteq M$ is a finite-dimensional $F$-vector space and a domain. For nonzero $x\in T$, multiplication by $x$ is an injective endomorphism of this finite-dimensional space, hence surjective; in particular $xy=1$ for some $y\in T$. Thus $T$ is a field containing $B$ and contained in $M=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$, so $T=M$. This proves the final finite-dimensionality assertion. The construction has preserved all specified residue identifications and, in equal characteristic, the chosen image of $t$ is exactly $\pi$.

I read the full statement of every cited node and checked each hypothesis against it. Step 1: c:C→A induces id_k, so it is local; it is injective in char 0 (up^n), and in char p it factors through k as a section. Step 2: the evaluation node's uniqueness clause gives surjectivity of k[[t]]→A, and injectivity uses F=t^nG with a unit residue. Step 3: adic lift with R=Z, I=J=pD, r=t=1. Step 4: k is perfect, so l/k satisfies def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension (2) via the separating-basis node, and the new node applies. Step 5: g is an A0-algebra map in both characteristics (the char p check uses s a section and t↦π↦0); b is local, and injective because b(p)≠0 or b(t)=π≠0. Step 6: qB=m_B^e, β-adic digits span B/qB, and separatedness plus completeness of D give the three 031D hypotheses. Step 7 is an elementary finite-domain argument. Every item clause is proved and no target was weakened; the perfect-core hypothesis is unused but kept. The new node lem-sfb-dvr-index-one-adic-formal-smoothness is exactly 09E7 (2)⇒(1), statement only, with notions defined or cited. I tested it on k[[t]]→l[[t]] and checked that the ramified and inseparable cases are excluded. It is not a duplicate: I grepped for 09E7, 07NQ and formally smooth with DVR terms.
